claims.text: Unmodified TC4 is an alpha-plus-beta dual-phase Ti-6Al-4V alloy.
TC4 has inherently low hardness and poor wear resistance that limit extreme-service and high-contact-stress use.
Approximately 3.5 kW is the optimal laser power for cladding the WNbMoTaV coating under the specified conditions.
Laser cladding at approximately 3.5 kW will produce a dense WNbMoTaV coating on TC4.
The coating will be metallurgically bonded to the TC4 substrate.
The coating will primarily comprise a high-strength BCC solid solution.
Substrate dilution will produce a minor Ti-rich phase in the coating.
Rapid solidification during laser cladding will refine the coating grains.
Lattice distortion in the BCC phase will increase resistance to plastic deformation.
Fine grains and grain-boundary strengthening will increase resistance to plastic deformation.
A protective tribo-oxide layer will form during sliding and reduce wear.
Excessively low laser power will cause incomplete melting and degrade coating performance.
Excessively high laser power will cause over-burning or excessive substrate dilution and degrade coating performance.
The approximately 3.5 kW coating will have higher surface microhardness than untreated TC4.
The approximately 3.5 kW coating will have lower wear-volume loss than untreated TC4 under identical testing conditions.
Bare TC4 has an average microhardness of approximately 341.25 HV0.3.
Bare TC4 has a wear-volume loss of approximately 6.09 × 10^7 cubic micrometres under the stated reciprocating-wear test.
The predicted improvement applies to coatings produced at 3.3, 3.5, and 3.7 kW under the specified processing and wear-test conditions.

contradictions.description: The stated microhardness test load is 0.98 N, which corresponds approximately to HV0.1, while the baseline and comparison threshold are reported as HV0.3, which conventionally uses about 2.94 N. Thus, the hypothesis does not consistently specify identical hardness-test conditions.
